first.rationale: Referral incentives have the clearest inherited evidence of adding qualified revenue without retention harm, aligning directly with sustainable long-term revenue while avoiding the known 30-day retention risk of promotional pricing. Verify referral economics and the strongest onboarding alternative before committing; the current activation and completion declines make onboarding simplification a credible competing use of the slot.

mid.rationale: Run a targeted referral-incentive experiment for accounts older than six months. The verified record shows +7% qualified revenue and +2% 30-day retention, directly supporting sustainable long-term qualified revenue. Shortened onboarding is a strong alternative and addresses current funnel deterioration, but its verified evidence is less direct on qualified revenue. Avoid promotional pricing despite competitive pressure because inherited evidence shows material retention harm.

final2.rationale: Respond with a tightly targeted, time-limited pricing test only for price-sensitive SMB accounts showing competitive churn risk. The deeper competitor cut and doubled churn conversations make inaction costly, while memory_73 indicates strong acquisition and revenue lift in this exact segment. Because that evidence also shows materially worse 30-day retention, do not broadly roll out; enforce retention and qualified-revenue guardrails and compare longer-term value against an untreated holdout.
